easy.q: Who did Elder Rasband say his message was for?
options: Everyone who is getting ready to serve a full-time mission
Everyone whose heart aches for loved ones who have turned from the Lord
Everyone who has just joined the Church and is learning the gospel
easy.why: Elder Rasband began by saying his message is for those whose hearts ache for loved ones who have turned away from the Lord. He said most of us have felt that ache in our families or among our friends.

easy.q: In the story of the prodigal son, what did the father do when he saw his son coming home, still a long way off?
options: He ran to him with compassion
He waited at the door for him
He sent a servant to meet him
easy.why: Elder Rasband quoted the Savior’s parable: “his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran [to him].” Heavenly Father reaches out to us with that same love.

easy.q: Elder Rasband said that, in everyday words, Jesus Christ says something to all who grieve. What is it?
options: “You can do it!”
“Keep on trying!”
“I’ve got this!”
easy.why: Elder Rasband said Jesus Christ says to all who grieve, “I’ve got this!” The Savior can carry what we cannot, so we can trust Him.

easy.q: In the Book of Mormon story Elder Rasband told, who prayed with much faith for Alma the Younger?
options: His friends, the sons of Mosiah
His father, Alma
His teacher, King Benjamin
easy.why: The angel told Alma the Younger that the Lord had heard the prayers of “his servant, Alma, who is thy father.” Elder Rasband said love is expressed in prayer.

easy.q: What did Elder Rasband ask us to do with our despair for loved ones who have strayed?
options: Turn it over to Jesus Christ
Keep it quietly to ourselves
Try harder to change them
easy.why: He said, “I ask you to turn over to Jesus Christ your despair for those wayward souls.” We cannot change hearts, but the Savior can.

medium.q: Elder Rasband listed things we do in our grief: preach, cajole, argue, demand, lecture. What did he say these efforts can do?
options: Slowly soften a loved one’s heart
Show loved ones we have not given up
Cause a greater rift with loved ones
Ease the guilt that we carry inside
medium.why: He said such efforts are “to no avail” and added, “If anything, these efforts can cause a greater rift.” That is why he pointed us to love and to the Savior instead.

medium.q: Elder Rasband quoted the Old Testament: “the battle is not yours, but God’s.” What was he using it to teach?
options: We should step back from our loved ones’ lives
Our loved ones’ choices matter less than we think
Stronger arguments for the truth will win in the end
The Savior can change hearts that we cannot change
medium.why: Just after the scripture, he asked us to turn our despair over to Jesus Christ and said, “We cannot change their hearts, but He can; He is a God of miracles.” Changing a heart is the Lord’s work.

medium.q: In Elder Rasband’s telling, what came to Alma the Younger from “somewhere deep within” before he cried to the Savior for mercy?
options: His father’s teachings of the coming of Jesus Christ
The angel’s words about his father’s many prayers
The good example of his friends, the sons of Mosiah
A scripture he had learned by heart as a young boy
medium.why: Elder Rasband said that from somewhere deep within “came his father’s teachings of the coming of Jesus Christ” to atone for the sins of the world. What a loving parent has taught can come back when it is most needed.

medium.q: According to Elder Rasband, what brought the prodigal son back home?
options: A promise he had made on leaving
Love, and he knew where to find it
Fear of what would come of him
A message his father had sent him
medium.why: Elder Rasband asked, “What brought him back?” and answered, “It was love. He knew where to find it.” Love is the answer to connecting with our loved ones.

medium.q: Elder Rasband’s first suggestion was to let go of any guilt. When did he say we fail?
options: When a loved one steps away from the Church
When our teaching at home was less than perfect
When we feel grief instead of feeling peace
Only when we give up and stop trying
medium.why: He taught, “We fail only when we give up and stop trying, so never, never give up on those you love.” He pointed to Alma, who kept praying for his son.

hard.q: Which situation best fits what Elder Rasband taught love is toward a loved one who has strayed?
options: A father says he now agrees with his daughter’s choices so there will be peace
A sister keeps her distance from her brother until he decides to come back
A mother stays interested in her son’s life and greets him with open arms
A friend sends a conference talk each week and urges him to watch it
hard.why: Elder Rasband said love is not “stepping back or sanctioning others’ decisions and actions.” It is being interested in their lives and “being there with arms outstretched and a cheerful countenance.”

hard.q: A grown son has stepped away from the Church. Which response by his mother best fits what Elder Rasband taught about agency and about not giving up?
options: She stops lecturing him, keeps praying for him, and leaves his heart to the Savior
She stops lecturing him and decides that his choices are no longer her concern
She keeps up the lectures, sure that enough reasoning will bring him back
She never speaks of faith again, certain that her own failures drove him away
hard.why: He taught, “By divine design, brothers and sisters, everyone must choose for themselves to follow Jesus Christ.” So we cannot change a heart, but the Savior can, and we “never, never give up on those you love.”

hard.q: According to Elder Rasband, what has the Savior already done for the loved ones for whom we grieve?
options: Removed the consequences of their choices
Promised that they will return in this life
Changed their hearts without their knowing
Paid for their sins and errant choices
hard.why: He said the Savior “has already paid for the sins and errant choices of all of God’s children, including those for whom you and I grieve.” He gave His life to bring them home.

hard.q: Elder Rasband quoted President Monson: “Never let a problem to be solved become more important than a person to be loved.” What does that ask of someone grieving a loved one’s choices?
options: Treat the loved one’s choices as no real problem at all
Put loving the person ahead of fixing what troubles us
Solve the problem first so that love can grow again
Avoid the subject so that the problem fades with time
hard.why: President Monson’s counsel puts the person first. It fits Elder Rasband’s teaching that love does not sanction wrong choices, yet stays interested in the person’s life with arms outstretched.

hard.q: As an Apostle, Elder Rasband made a promise about the storms that pull loved ones off course. What exactly did he promise?
options: Loved ones will come back soon if we stay faithful
Storms will pass by families who pray mightily
The storm cannot drag you down if you are built on Christ
Grief will leave as soon as we let go of guilt
hard.why: His promise was to those who grieve: the storm “shall have no power” to drag you down “because of the rock upon which ye are built.” He added, “If that rock is Jesus Christ.”
